A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same ProOPF study. Their main text, equations, figures, tables, and appendices are readable and support comparison, including matching retained material across renumbering and relocation.

before.justification: v1 reports original LLM evaluations and supervised fine-tuning results on ProOPF-B in Section 6 and Table 1, with additional model results in Appendix H.

after.justification: v4 retains those empirical results and adds scaling, generalization, enhanced-prompt, and Llama fine-tuning experiments in Sections 6.4–6.6 and Appendix H.

M1.justification: The modification-based representation, scenario-tree synthesis, filtering algorithms, and core fine-tuning approach remain unchanged. Section 6.6 adds a limited inference adaptation: GPT-5.2 and Claude 4.5 Sonnet receive solver instructions, reference implementations, and parameter-mapping guidance through enhanced prompts.

E1.justification: The original 12K training dataset, 121-case benchmark, four task levels, and base-system pool remain unchanged. Appendix H.1 substantially extends evaluation beyond the original conditions to unseen grid architectures and novel operational scenarios generated from extended scenario trees, covering Levels 1, 2, and 4.

E2.justification: The comparator sets in Table 1 and the extended model table are retained. Appendix H.3 adds Llama-3.1-8B without fine-tuning as a comparator for its fine-tuned counterpart; Table 4 adds comparisons between original and enhanced prompting for GPT-5.2 and Claude 4.5 Sonnet.

E3.justification: New protocols include balanced 4K/8K/12K training subsets, training with versus without Level 4, additional OOD samples numbering 36/30/26 across Levels 1/2/4, and fine-tuning an 8B Llama backbone. Appendix E also substantively revises previously printed evaluation prompts. These are reported protocol additions and revisions; unchanged original result tables do not establish that those experiments were rerun.

E4.justification: Beyond v1's existing failure diagnostics and prompting comparisons, v4 adds analyses of training-data scaling, compositional transfer without Level-4 supervision, robustness to unseen systems and scenarios, sensitivity to solver-oriented prompt support, and transfer of fine-tuning benefits across model families.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-run counts, random seeds, confidence intervals, error bars, or statistical significance tests for model performance. The added experiments continue reporting point estimates.

E6.justification: Table 1 and v1 Table 9, retained as v4 Table 13, have unchanged scores. New results include Level-4 few-shot accuracy of 3.84% without Level-4 training versus 11.54% with it, and enhanced-prompt Level-4 scores of 26.92% for GPT-5.2 and 23.08% for Claude. OOD, scaling, and Llama results are also added. However, v4 Table 2 assigns the full-data Level-2/3 scores as 20.70%/33.30%, reversing Table 1's 33.30%/20.70%.

T1.justification: The OPF formulations, modification-space definitions, synthesis equations, and six capability-metric definitions are retained. Appendix B's mathematical formulations and the synthesis and evaluation algorithms are unchanged apart from presentation. No new theorem or proof is introduced.

C1.justification: The abstract and three stated contributions retain the same claims: a professional OPF dataset and benchmark, modification-based multilevel synthesis, and concrete/abstract execution-based evaluation. The central conclusion about difficulties with semantic inference and structural modeling remains; new experiments mainly support and qualify these claims.

C2.justification: v4 adds interpretations concerning transferable inference beyond scenario memorization, the importance of explicit Level-4 supervision, and recovery of performance through solver-oriented context. It also discusses cross-backbone portability and adds stated limitations concerning transmission-level scope, intermediate-step validation, and insufficient complex-task training data.

D1.justification: New Appendix E.4 supplies a complete Level-4 benchmark example, executable function, two parameter instantiations with execution results, and zero/few-shot prompts. Existing prompt instructions are also revised. The generation pseudocode, original Qwen training hyperparameters and hardware, and main code/data repository link remain unchanged.

R1.justification: The introduction strengthens the real-time dispatch motivation with references including Jabr and Gao, replaces the Carpentier citation with Babiker, and adds power-system references in Appendix A. References including Bai, Wu's Evo-Step, and Xu are removed. The central positioning against coarse-grained optimization benchmarks remains unchanged.

P1.justification: v4 rewrites parts of the introduction and evaluation prompts, adds experimental subsections and limitations, and subdivides Appendix H. Author/header text is corrected, with affiliations and acknowledgements added. Most existing prose and the overall methodological narrative retain their structure.

P2.justification: New Tables 2–4, 12, and 14 substantially expand the experimental displays to cover scaling, compositional transfer, prompt enhancement, OOD evaluation, and cross-backbone fine-tuning. Existing figures and result tables are retained. Appendix tables and prompt boxes are reflowed, and the placeholder running header is replaced with the paper title.

improvement.justification: The added generalization, supervision, prompt-support, and second-backbone experiments strengthen aspects of validation absent from v1, while Appendix E.4 improves reproducibility. These benefits are limited by the new Table 2/Table 1 score inconsistency and incomplete specification of the OOD cases and enhanced-prompt setup. Overall, the evidence and documentation improve, but the new analyses are not sufficiently consistent and reproducible to establish a major quality gain.
